cards.title: Clean As You Go
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- say what "clean as you go" means
- do it in practice during a shift
- explain why it is everyone's job

cards.title: Little and often
cards.body: "Clean as you go" is the habit of cleaning and tidying continuously while you work, rather than letting mess pile up to deal with later. It keeps your area safe, hygienic and under control, and it makes service run far more smoothly.

cards.title: What goes wrong
cards.body: Think about what happens when you do not clean as you go. Then at the end of service you face a mountain of cleaning when you are already tired.

items.title: Bacteria and allergens
items.text: Dirty boards and surfaces spread them.

items.title: Big end clean
items.text: A mountain when you are tired.

cards.title: Four habits
cards.body: Little and often is always easier.

cards.title: So the next person can find it
cards.body: Put tools, ingredients and stock back where they belong once you have finished with them. The next person can find them and the area stays clear.

left.title: Do
items: Return tools and stock to their place

right.title: Do not
items: Leave things where you used them

cards.title: Not just the cleaners or the KP
cards.body: A clean, tidy area is safer for the whole team, more hygienic for our guests, and looks far more professional if a guest glances behind the bar or into the kitchen.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Wipe spills the moment they happen
- Clear rubbish as you create it
- Clean and sanitise surfaces between tasks
- Put tools and stock back where they belong
- It is everyone's job

cards.q: What does "clean as you go" mean?
options: Cleaning and tidying as you work
A full clean at the end of the week
Cleaning when a manager asks you to
cards.why: It is the habit of cleaning continuously while you work, not leaving mess until later.

cards.q: Spills should be wiped up the moment they happen.
cards.why: Spills sit on the floor and become slip hazards, so wipe them at once.

cards.q: Between different tasks, surfaces should be…
cards.why: Clean and sanitise surfaces between tasks so bacteria and allergens do not spread.

cards.q: Cleaning as you go helps prevent slips and cross-contamination.
cards.why: It stops spills becoming slip hazards and dirty surfaces spreading bacteria and allergens.

cards.q: Whose responsibility is "clean as you go"?
cards.why: It is everyone's job, not just the cleaners' or the KP's.

cards.q: Letting mess build up until the end of service is the easiest approach.
cards.why: It leaves a mountain of cleaning when you are tired. Little and often is easier.

cards.q: What should you do with tools and stock once you've finished with them?
options: Leave them nearby for next time
Put them back where they belong
Leave them for the next shift to sort
cards.why: Put them back so the next person can find them and the area stays clear.
A tidy area is safer for the team, more hygienic for guests and looks more professional.

cards.q: "Little and often" cleaning is easier than one big clean at the end.
cards.why: Cleaning in small steps all the way through is always easier.

cards.q: Name one problem caused by NOT cleaning as you go.
cards.why: Slip hazards, bacteria and allergens spreading, clutter and a huge end-of-service clean all follow.
